chunks: They are nothing but carrier-beasts laden with sins and camels laden with evil deeds. I swear and again swear that the Umayyads will have to spit out the caliphate as phlegm is spat and there after they will never taste it nor relish its flavour so long as day and night rotate.

key_terms.أُمَيَّةُ: Umayyads (referring to the clan or the caliphate)
key_terms.الْجَدِيدَانِ: the two new things (day and night)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the Umayyads and their rule?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) characterizes the Umayyads as mere vehicles for carrying sins, swearing that they will eventually be forced to relinquish the caliphate in a manner as involuntary as spitting out phlegm. This vivid metaphor underscores the transient and distasteful nature of their rule, which will persist only as long as the cycle of day and night continues, highlighting the impermanence of their political dominance.
